findings.evidence: The bridge is immediate: `CompletelyMonotoneOn.iff_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg isOpen_Ioi.uniqueDiffOn` (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/TangentCone/Basic.lean:291 `IsOpen.uniqueDiffOn`) plus `iteratedDerivWithin_of_isOpen` (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/IteratedDeriv/Defs.lean:318, `EqOn (iteratedDerivWithin n f s) (iteratedDeriv n f) s` for open `s`) identifies the two sign conditions on `Ioi 0`.
findings.fix: Add `isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi_iff_completelyMonotoneOn : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f ↔ CompletelyMonotoneOn f (Ioi 0)` and replace the bodies of `IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.add`/`.smul` with `CompletelyMonotoneOn.add`/`.smul` transported through it, as done at lines 274 and 280.
findings.issue: `IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi` is the special case `CompletelyMonotoneOn f (Ioi 0)`, yet `add` (378) and `smul` (388) are still proved by hand at the `iteratedDeriv` level — the same duplication that was removed for `IsCompletelyMonotone.add`/`.smul` (274, 280) in this PR, left in place for the other half-line predicate.

findings.evidence: grep over `TauCeti/` for `absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg` returns only the declaration itself (Basic.lean:197-198); its proof body (199-203) is `rw [isCompletelyMonotone_iff_completelyMonotoneOn, CompletelyMonotoneOn]` plus the set identity.
findings.fix: Delete it; the general statement is `CompletelyMonotoneOn f s ↔ AbsolutelyMonotoneOn (fun u => f (-u)) (-s)`, which is `Iff.rfl` from the new `def`. No compatibility shim is needed.
findings.issue: `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg` is now just `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_completelyMonotoneOn` (189) composed with `-(Ici 0) = Iic 0`, i.e. the `s = Ici 0` instance of the new definition, and it has no uses anywhere in the repo — duplicated API at a strictly less general level.

summary: The new `CompletelyMonotoneOn` sits at the right level and `IsCompletelyMonotone.add`/`.smul` now derive from it, but the same derivation was not applied to the open-half-line predicate, whose `add`/`smul` remain hand-proved duplicates of the general result. The `Iic 0` reflection lemma is now a redundant specialization of the new definition.
